tagline: Blasted from limestone for carriages, and shut to cars again.
intro: From The Paseo at Independence Avenue, Cliff Drive winds through Kessler Park under limestone bluffs that look down on the East Bottoms and the Missouri River, and ends at Indian Mound on Gladstone Boulevard. John Mahoney's crews blasted the roadbed out of solid rock, with drops of more than 200 feet in places, and it opened in 1900 as the centerpiece of the park, a cornerstone of George Kessler's parks and boulevards.

Kessler meant it for quiet carriage rides and worried about automobile speed-maniacs. In 1903, after a car spooked a horse, the park board banned motor vehicles, and the Kansas City Automobile Club got the ban repealed. The motorcars are shut out again now.

moments.title: Carl J. DiCapo Fountain
moments.text: The spring where pioneers and the Scarritt family once cooled their milk and butter went dry, and in 1989 a 40-foot artificial waterfall and reflecting pool went in where it had been.

moments.title: The Colonnade
moments.text: Henry Wright's 1908 Beaux-Arts pavilion on The Concourse was built for admiring the landscape, and the neighborhood has since adopted it as Kansas City's biggest front porch.

practical: Cliff Drive is closed to motorized vehicles.
